     continues to grow and currently serves the following schools:

         • 1 K-8 Magnet School
         • 14 Elementary Schools
         • 5 Middle Schools
         • 3 High Schools

                                                   7
                                             SCOPE OF PROPOSAL
                                  Speaker Cabling Riverdale Ridge High School


1. Project Overview

School District 27J is soliciting proposals from qualified low-voltage cabling contractors to provide labor, materials,
installation, termination, labeling, testing, and documentation for new speaker cabling within an existing District 27J
school building, Riverdale Ridge High School.

The purpose of this project is to replace the existing classroom speaker daisy-chain wiring configuration with a
dedicated home-run cabling configuration. Each classroom speaker shall be individually wired back to the nearest
designated MDF/IDF location.

The existing classroom speakers will remain in place. The current speaker model is Bogen CSD 1X2. The speaker
specification sheet and installation manual are included with this RFP and shall be reviewed by the contractor prior
to submitting a proposal.

2. Project Scope

The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, supervision, and incidental work necessary to complete
the speaker cabling installation described in this Scope of Work and the associated drawings.

The work shall include:

    •    Installation of new 18/2 shielded speaker cable from each designated classroom to the nearest MDF/IDF
         location identified on the project drawings.
    •    Installation of one individual cable run for each classroom.
    •    Removal, abandonment, or modification of existing daisy-chain cabling as directed by the District.
    •    Routing of cabling through existing building pathways where available and appropriate.
    •    Installation of all required dedicated cable support infrastructure.
    •    Proper termination of all speaker cable conductors at the designated termination points.
    •    Labeling of each cable with the corresponding classroom/room number.
    •    Testing and verification of installed cabling.
    •    Cleanup and restoration of work areas following each installation phase.
    •    Coordination with District personnel and other contractors as required to complete the work.

3. Cable Requirements

Unless otherwise noted, all new classroom speaker cabling shall meet the following requirements:

    •    18/2 shielded speaker cable.
    •    Cable shall be suitable for the intended public address/speaker application.
    •    Cable shall be installed in accordance with the cable manufacturer's requirements and applicable codes.
    •    Cable shall be installed as a continuous run from the classroom speaker location to the designated
         MDF/IDF termination location.
    •    Cable shall not be spliced.
    •    Cable shall not contain unterminated conductors or elements.
    •    Conductors shall be terminated only at designated outlets, terminals, or equipment termination points.
    •    Cable shall be installed without excessive tension and within the manufacturer's specified bending radius.
    •    Cable shall not be bruised, kinked, scored, deformed, crushed, or abraded.

                                                          8
    •    Any cable damaged during installation shall be removed and replaced with new cable at the contractor's
         expense.

4. Cable Support and Pathways

All cabling shall be supported using dedicated cable support infrastructure.

The contractor shall furnish and install all support infrastructure required for a complete and code-compliant
installation, including, but not limited to:

    •    J-hooks
    •    Cable slings
    •    Cable straps
    •    Cable tray
    •    Conduit
    •    Manufactured sleeves
    •    Other approved cable support systems

Cabling shall not be supported by other trade's equipment or architectural elements.

Under no circumstances shall speaker cabling be supported by:

    •    HVAC ducts
    •    HVAC piping
    •    Plumbing piping
    •    Electrical conduit
    •    Electrical equipment
    •    Existing unrelated cabling
    •    Ceiling tile
    •    Ceiling grid
    •    Light fixtures
    •    Sprinkler piping
    •    Structural elements not specifically approved for cable support
    •    Other building systems or architectural elements

The contractor shall provide sufficient dedicated support infrastructure to maintain the cable installation in a neat,
secure, and code-compliant manner.

5. Cable Routing and Installation

Cables shall be neatly routed and trained to their respective termination points.

The contractor shall:

    •    Bundle, lace, and train conductors as appropriate.
    •    Install lacing bars and distribution spools where required.
    •    Maintain manufacturer's minimum bend radius requirements.
    •    Avoid excessive tension on cable.
    •    Maintain separation from sources of electrical interference as required.
    •    Protect cable where passing through walls, floors, sleeves, raceways, or other penetrations.
    •    Provide appropriate fire-rated sleeves and sealing where required.
    •    Maintain the integrity of existing fire-rated assemblies.

                                                           9
    •    Coordinate penetrations and pathway requirements with the District prior to installation.

Any penetrations created by the contractor shall be properly sleeved, sealed, and fire stopped as required by
applicable codes.

6. Speaker Equipment

The existing classroom speakers shall remain in place.

The existing speaker model is: Bogen CSD 1X2

The contractor shall review the Bogen CSD 1X2 specification sheet and installation documentation included with
this RFP to ensure that the proposed cabling installation is compatible with the existing speaker equipment.

Unless specifically identified as an alternate or change by the District, the contractor shall not replace the existing
classroom speakers.

7. MDF/IDF Termination

Each classroom speaker cable shall be routed to the MDF/IDF identified on the associated drawings.

The contractor shall:

    •    Route each cable to the designated MDF/IDF.
    •    Maintain organized cable routing within the MDF/IDF.
    •    Provide appropriate cable management.
    •    Label each cable at the MDF/IDF termination point.
    •    Leave sufficient cable for proper termination and future service.
    •    Maintain appropriate bend radius and cable management within the MDF/IDF.

This RFP does not include connection of the new speaker cabling to the Bogen PA system head-end
equipment.

The District or its designated PA contractor will be responsible for connecting the new speaker cabling to the Bogen
PA system and completing associated system configuration/programming.

8. Cable Labeling

Each speaker cable shall be clearly and permanently identified.

The contractor shall label the cable with the corresponding classroom/room number at both ends of the cable:

    1.   At the classroom speaker termination point.
    2.   At the MDF/IDF termination point.

Labels shall consist of vinyl wraparound labels or self-adhesive labels suitable for telecommunications/low-voltage
cabling applications.

Labels shall be legible, securely attached, and resistant to normal environmental conditions.

Room identification shall correspond exactly with the room numbers shown on the project drawings.

9. Phasing and Installation Schedule
                                                            10
The project shall be completed in phases by building wing.

Installation work will be scheduled across multiple Monday installation dates. The building does not have
regularly scheduled classes on Mondays, and Mondays will be utilized as the primary installation period to minimize
disruption to instructional activities.

The contractor shall coordinate the installation schedule with District 27J prior to beginning work.

The contractor shall:

    •    Coordinate installation dates with the District.
    •    Complete work by wing or designated installation area.
    •    Maintain safe access through the building during installation.
    •    Coordinate access to classrooms, MDFs, and IDFs.
    •    Notify the District of any conditions that may affect the installation schedule.
    •    Maintain a clean and safe work environment at the conclusion of each Monday installation period.

The District reserves the right to establish the sequence and timing of individual installation phases.

10. Coordination with District

The successful contractor shall coordinate all work with the District's designated project representative.

Prior to beginning work in each wing, the contractor shall verify:

    •    Classroom locations.
    •    MDF/IDF serving each classroom.
    •    Cable pathways.
    •    Existing conditions.
    •    Access requirements.
    •    Any conflicts with other building systems.
    •    Required penetrations and pathway infrastructure.

Any discrepancy between the drawings and field conditions shall be brought to the District's attention before
proceeding with affected work.

11. Existing Conditions

The building is an existing occupied school facility. Contractors shall account for existing construction, building
systems, and conditions when developing their proposal.

The contractor shall verify field conditions prior to installation.

The contractor shall take appropriate precautions to protect:

    •    Existing PA equipment.
    •    Existing speaker equipment.
    •    Network equipment.
    •    Telecommunications equipment.
    •    Electrical equipment.
    •    Building finishes.
    •    Ceiling systems.
    •    HVAC systems.
                                                            11
    •    Other building systems.

The contractor shall be responsible for repairing damage caused by its work.

12. Cleanup

The contractor shall maintain a clean and orderly work area throughout the project.

At the conclusion of each installation period, the contractor shall:

    •    Remove cable scraps and installation debris.
    •    Remove unused materials and packaging.
    •    Clean work areas.
    •    Replace ceiling tiles and other temporarily displaced building components.
    •    Leave classrooms, hallways, MDFs, IDFs, and other work areas in the same or better condition than they
         were found.

13. Codes, Standards, and Workmanship

All work shall comply with applicable federal, state, and local codes, ordinances, regulations, and industry
standards.

The contractor shall perform all work in a professional manner consistent with generally accepted low-voltage
cabling practices.

The completed installation shall be neat, organized, properly supported, properly labeled, and suitable for long-term
maintenance and service.

14. Contractor-Furnished Materials

Unless specifically identified otherwise in the proposal documents, the contractor shall furnish all labor, materials,
tools, equipment, lifts, ladders, cable support hardware, pathway materials, fasteners, sleeves, firestopping materials,
labels, termination hardware, and other incidental materials necessary to complete the work.

15. Proposal Requirements

Proposals shall clearly identify all costs associated with completing the work described in this Scope of Work.

At a minimum, proposals shall include:

    •    Total project cost.
    •    Labor costs.
    •    Material costs.
    •    Proposed 18/2 shielded speaker cable manufacturer and part number.
    •    Description of proposed cable support infrastructure.
    •    Proposed installation schedule.
    •    Estimated number of Monday installation dates required.
    •    Lead time for materials.
    •    Warranty information.
    •    Any exclusions or assumptions.
    •    Identification of any proposed deviations from this Scope of Work.


                                                           12
The District may request clarification of any proposed exclusions, assumptions, or deviations prior to contract
award.

16. Exclusions

The following items are specifically excluded from this RFP unless identified as an approved alternate:

    •    Connection to the Bogen PA system head-end equipment.
    •    Programming or configuration of the Bogen PA system.
    •    Replacement of existing Bogen CSD 1X2 classroom speakers.
    •    Replacement of Bogen head-end equipment.
    •    PA system commissioning beyond cable testing and verification.
    •    Changes to PA system programming or software.
    •    Repair or replacement of unrelated existing PA system components.

Any work outside of the defined scope must receive written approval from District 27J prior to commencement.

17. Drawings and Reference Documents

The following documents are incorporated into this RFP and shall be considered part of the project requirements:

    •    Project drawings identifying classroom quantities and MDF/IDF locations by wing.
    •    Bogen CSD 1X2 speaker specification sheet.
    •    Bogen CSD 1X2 speaker installation manual.

Contractors shall review all provided documentation prior to submitting a proposal.

18. Acceptance of Work

The District will inspect completed work for compliance with this Scope of Work.

Acceptance will be based on, at minimum:

    •    Correct cable routing.
    •    Individual home-run cabling for each classroom.
    •    Proper cable support.
    •    Proper terminations.
    •    Proper labeling.
    •    Compliance with applicable codes and installation requirements.
    •    Successful cable testing.
    •    Completion of required documentation.
    •    Acceptable workmanship and cleanup.

Any deficiencies identified by the District shall be corrected by the contractor at no additional cost to the District.

                                  Bogen CSD 1X2 Speaker Specifications Sheet




Drop-In Ceiling Speaker
CSD1X2 & Variations with Back Can
Bogen’s CSD1X2 Drop-In Ceiling Speakers are 1' X 2'
speakers that allow for fast and easy installation.
Just make one simple cut to the ceiling tile, lay the
support rail crossbar (included) across the ceiling
grid, and drop the speaker into place.

• Finely perforated grille over the entire front of speaker
• Fully enclosed, industrial grade steel construction
• Enclosed Back Can
• 8'' main cone with secondary high-frequency cone
• 70V/25V, 4-watt transformer (4, 2, 1, 0.5, 0.25 watt) taps;
  selected by rotary switch
• Seismic attachment point                                                                                 CEILING TILE

• Available in off-white and bright white (“U” versions)
  grille finish                                                           CSD1X2                           CEILING GRID
• ''VR'' versions have a Recessed Volume Control
   (front-mounted)                                                                  SUPPORT RAIL CROSSBAR (included)

• Listed to UL Standard 1480 for U.S. use                       *Listed to UL Standard 1480 for U.S. use
• Support Rail Crossbar (included)

    Architect and Engineer Specifications
   The speaker shall be a Bogen Model CSD1X2. It shall be a 1 ft. x 2 ft. steel assembly with non-reflective, finished metal grille; damped high-
   compliance factory-mounted 8" loudspeaker with a treated paper cone; and 70V/25V transformer. The 8" main speaker cone shall have a
   10 ounce magnet. A secondary high frequency cone speaker shall be included in the assembly. The back of the assembly shall have a back
   can enclosure. The speaker shall include a seismic attachment point. Output shall be 94 dB @ 1W/1m (min.). Frequency response shall be
   110 Hz to 20 kHz (min.). Transformer shall have power taps of 4, 2, 1, 0.5, and 0.25 watts, selectable by rotary switch. A support rail cross-
   bar shall be included. The speaker shall measure 12-1/4" W x 5" H x 24" D. The speaker shall weigh 10 lb. Speaker listed to UL Standard
   1480 for U.S. use.
   For CSD1X2: Front grille shall be off-white in color.
   For CSD1X2U: Front grille finish shall be bright white in color.
   For CSD1X2VR: Front grille finish shall be off-white in color. An easily accessible, front-mounted recessed volume control shall be included.
                                                                                                 For CSD1X2VRU: Front grille finish shall be bright white in color. An easily accessible, front-mount-
                                                                                                 ed recessed volume control shall be included.

70V & 25V Speaker Systems
Electrical Connection
1. Remove electrical box cover, then install
   cable clamp (if desired) and feed interconnecting
   cable into the electrical box.
2. Select speaker leads for desired system type:
   70V - Red, 25V - Yellow, and COM - Black                                    KN
   for both. Interconnect the speakers in the
                                                                               FEED
   system, making sure that all leads of the same                              CABLE
   color are connected together. Avoid swapping colors.
3. Cut bare wire tip off of unused speaker lead. Secure
   all mechanical connections and re-install
   electrical box cover.
4. Set tap selector switch to proper tap setting.
NOTE: All wiring must comply with NFPA 70

Ceiling Installation
1. For 2 ft. x 4 ft. tile space, cut ceiling tile to 35-1/2'' long.                            70V            Red
   For 2 ft. x 2 ft. tile space, cut to 11-1/2"Iong.
                                                                                               25V            Yellow
2. Place speaker in ceiling opening.
3. Slide Tile Support Rail under speaker edge beside opening.                                  COM            Black
4. Drop in
